description: Returns what the PLATFORM says happened to a post, plus `post_id` once it is live and `fail_reason` when it is not. Statuses: `prepared` (staged, nothing sent), `scheduled` (due at `scheduled_at`; `schedule_custody` says whether aicut or the platform holds it), `submitted` (handed to aicut's YouTube or Instagram poster, nothing confirmed), `publishing` (TikTok took the job and is fetching the file), `posted`, `draft_sent` (a TikTok draft is in the user's TikTok inbox: they finish and post it there, it is NOT live), `failed` and `unconfirmed`. `unconfirmed` MEANS WE DO NOT KNOW and is terminal: the post was sent and its outcome never learned, so it may be live under the user's name: tell them to check the account and do NOT publish it again (it could double-post). WHEN: after `publish_post`. `posted` is reported only when the platform confirms the post exists: `publishing` or `submitted` has not gone out yet, however long it has been. TIMING: TikTok usually takes under a minute, YouTube and Instagram (aicut's poster) one to five minutes. Poll about every 10 seconds, with no timers or background shells. 403 `insufficient_scope` = the user's connection lacks the `social:publish` permission: not a bad `video_id` or `account_id`, and a retry cannot fix it. Tell them to disconnect and reconnect aicut at https://www.aicut.pro/account/settings#connections (the full steps are in `prepare_post`'s REFUSALS), then STOP. A 403 here says nothing about the POST: one that went out stays live, unreadable until the user reconnects. Read-only: posts nothing.
name: get_post_status
title: Get a post's status
